analysis: Both changed files are test-only Swift sources. The sole change in each is the stub LanguageModel's prepare signature, from (input, cache, windowSize) to (input, cache, state: LMOutput.State?, prefill: PrefillParameters). The new signature tracks an upstream MLXLMCommon protocol change. See FlintReasoningVisibilityTests.swift line 316 (inside #if DEBUG) and StandaloneServerModelAdmissionTests.swift line 20. The stubs still return .tokens(input.text) and an empty newCache. No production code, authorization, attestation, encryption, key handling, cache storage or billing path is touched. The tests' existing assertions are unchanged: Flint reasoning withholding, usage and billing counts, response-hash commitment to emitted bytes (TB-007), and standalone model admission and eviction. The signature change does not weaken any of them. The ProviderCore production code that consumes the new protocol (the dependency bump and any production LanguageModel conformances) is not in this batch, so I could not check it. Nothing here shows a regression for T-041, T-008 or other threat IDs. Residual question for integration: whether the matching production-side signature and dependency changes in other batches affect security-relevant behavior, such as prefill state handling or cache reuse. These test files do not show that.
